title: Your LLM Deception Monitor Is Broken. The Fix Is in the Training Data - Sachin Kumar, LexisNexis
talk_summary: The speaker presents a research method for detecting backdoors (sleeper agents) in fine-tuned LLMs by computing activation deltas between base and fine-tuned checkpoints and training a sparse autoencoder on the difference (diff-SAE), which isolates the backdoor as a single interpretable feature. The talk is about safety/security monitoring of model weights, not about agent orchestration, review quality, or cost efficiency.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run identical probe inputs through base and fine-tuned checkpoints, subtract activations (delta-A), train a small sparse autoencoder on the delta at one middle layer, and gate the build if the top backdoor feature fires.
takeaways.evidence_quote: For each input, run it through both models, and subtract the base activations from the fine-tuned ones. That's what we call as delta A.
takeaways.numbers: Backdoor isolation score 0.4 vs ~0.01 for joint cross-coders (40x gap); precision 1.0 with zero false positives; single feature catches ~25% of triggers; 4x SAE matches 32x with 8x fewer features.

takeaways.technique: Behavioral evals are blind to conditional triggers
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues that green evals and behavioral monitors cannot catch behavior that only fires on an untested trigger, so a structural/weight-level signal is needed alongside behavioral testing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You cannot test your way out of this, which is exactly the problem.
